mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a decline in 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return remains positive despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 5.25%, or the 5.25% threshold is not met for ≥3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 3.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of slower wage growth and reduced corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 3.5% and remains above for ≥2 months
failure_condition: In a regime where UNRATE > 3.5% for ≥6 months, the 20-day forward return is non-negative on average, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a two-sample test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (units of housing starts) by at least 10% relative to the prior month predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals renewed builder confidence and economic expansion.
regime_hint: Early stage of housing cycle expansion
failure_condition: Over 12 consecutive months with HOUST ≥10% monthly gains, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO (index of industrial production) of at least 2% in two consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side momentum, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During regimes where INDPRO declines <2% for ≥4 consecutive months, the 20-day forward return is non-negative on average.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise simultaneously by at least 0.25% in the same month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns positive due to expectations of future rate hikes and higher inflation.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS ↑ ≥0.25% AND CPIAUCSL ↑ ≥0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: In 100 such co-movement events, the 20-day forward return is negative in >70% of cases, or the interaction coefficient is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 2,000 since the last peak is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals labor market recovery momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2,000 since the prior monthly peak
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 5-day forward return is negative in >50% of instances where PAYEMS meets the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly RSAFS (retail sales) decline of more than 5% from the prior month, occurring during a period of UNRATE < 3%, predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to demand destruction.
regime_hint: Demand contraction in slack labor market
failure_condition: In 10 such events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically worse than baseline (p > 0.05), or the interaction effect is insignificant.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds its 12-month high by at least 2%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns positive, reflecting optimism about future demand.
candidate_trigger: 3-month GDPC1 MA crosses above 12-month high by ≥2%
failure_condition: In regimes where this condition holds for ≥4 consecutive 3-month windows, the 20-day forward return remains non-positive on average.
